2027-01-23.title: Third Saturday of Denha
2027-01-23.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Striving side by side for the faith of the gospel
The faith of the Canaanite woman
2027-01-23.alt: Season of Denha. Church Unity Octave.
2027-01-23.verse: Then Jesus answered her, “Woman, great is your faith! Let it be done for you as you wish.” And her daughter was healed instantly.
theo: Paul writes to the Philippians from prison with one wish: “live your life in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ”, so that he may hear that they are “standing firm in one spirit, striving side by side with one mind for the faith of the gospel, and are in no way intimidated by your opponents.” He even calls suffering a gift: “he has graciously granted you the privilege not only of believing in Christ, but of suffering for him as well”. In this Unity Octave his words are a plan for all Christians: not rivals, but companions side by side for the one Gospel.

The Gospel shows a faith that will not give up. A Canaanite woman, a foreigner, cries: “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David; my daughter is tormented by a demon.” Jesus does not answer; the disciples want her sent away; Jesus says he was sent to the lost sheep of Israel. She kneels: “Lord, help me.” Even the hard saying about the children's food does not stop her: “Yes, Lord, yet even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters’ table.” Jesus replies: “Woman, great is your faith! Let it be done for you as you wish.” Denha celebrates Christ revealed to the nations; here a pagan mother teaches the disciples what faith looks like: humble, persistent, and sure that a crumb from Christ is enough.
outline: Ask: have you ever kept asking God when the answer seemed to be no?
A life that matches what we believe.
One spirit, one mind, one Gospel.

2027-01-23.prayer: Lord Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on us. Give us the faith of the Canaanite woman, humble and persistent, and help us to live in a manner worthy of your Gospel, standing firm in one spirit with all who believe in you. Amen.
altar: Like the Canaanite woman we come to the Holy Qurbana knowing we are unworthy, and Christ gives us not crumbs but himself, the Bread of Life.

family.explain: A mother from another country begged Jesus to heal her daughter. Even when it seemed Jesus said no, she kept asking. Jesus said: woman, great is your faith! And her daughter was healed.
family.intention: We pray for Christians of all Churches, that we may be one.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing we will keep asking Jesus for, every day, as a family?”

illus: A mother in Kannur prayed every evening for twelve years for her son, who was lost in drink. Relatives told her to stop wasting her breath. She answered: even the dogs eat the crumbs; I am only asking for a crumb. One Easter her son walked into the parish church and asked for confession. She says she still prays the same prayer, now for other mothers.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on us. Give us a faith that does not give up. Amen.
share: Live your life in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ (Philippians 1:27). Where does my life not match my faith?
Lord, help me (Matthew 15:25). What do I need to keep asking for?
Woman, great is your faith! (Matthew 15:28). Would Jesus say this of my faith?
interc: For all Christians, that we may strive side by side for the Gospel.
For parents praying for their children.
For those who feel God is silent.
For Christians who suffer for their faith.
For our group, that our faith may be humble and persistent.
pm.close: Father, you hear the cry of every nation. Grant us the faith of the Canaanite woman and the unity Paul prayed for. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Paul writes from prison to the Philippians: live your life in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ, standing firm in one spirit, striving side by side with one mind for the faith of the gospel (Philippians 1:27). In this Unity Octave, that is God's word to all Christians.
He even says that suffering for Christ is a privilege, a gift of grace (Philippians 1:29). Christians who suffer together for the Gospel discover how much unites them.

In the Gospel a Canaanite woman cries: have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David. Jesus does not answer. The disciples want her sent away. She kneels and says only: Lord, help me (Matthew 15:25). And when Jesus speaks of the children's food, she answers: yes, Lord, yet even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters' table.

Jesus says: woman, great is your faith! (Matthew 15:28). She is a foreigner, yet she shows the disciples what faith is: humble, persistent, sure that a crumb from Christ is enough. When God seems silent, let us not give up. Let us say with her: Lord, help me. Amen.
kids: Children, a mother kept asking Jesus to help her sick daughter, even when it seemed he said no. Jesus said: great is your faith! Let us never stop praying. Say with her today: Lord, help me!
